- If sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slightly, especially after spikes.
- If sentiment is strongly negative (≤ 0.33) or volatile, model underestimates; increase forecast to account for risk reversal or mean reversion.
- After a sharp price spike, model often overshoots; apply a downward correction of 1–3% in next 3–5 days.
- When true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days above 80), model fails to adjust; reduce forecast slope toward historical mean.
- If model forecast is flat or rising slowly while sentiment is rising, model underestimates volatility; add 0.5–1.5% upward bias for next 3–7 days.
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 0.67, 0.33, 0.67), model often misjudges direction; use sentiment-weighted average of recent 3–5 days for smoothing.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overfits recent trend; apply 1–2% downward bias if sentiment is neutral or slightly negative.
